transcript.heading: News Report One (British Male)
paras: The British government has announced new funding for international student exchange programs, allocating an additional 80 million pounds to support study abroad opportunities over the next three years. The funding will enable over 40,000 students from UK universities to spend a semester or full academic year at partner institutions across Europe, Asia, and North America. Education officials state that the program aims to improve cultural understanding, foreign language skills, and global employability among British graduates. Priority will be given to students from low-income backgrounds who might not otherwise have the financial means to study overseas. The new initiative comes as a replacement for the Erasmus+ program, which the UK left following Brexit. Universities have welcomed the announcement, though some have noted that the funding level is still significantly below what was available through the previous European scheme.
Questions 1 and 2 are based on the news report you have just heard.

2. Who will receive priority for the exchange program?

transcript.heading: News Report Two (American Female)
paras: Public schools across the state of California are implementing a new mandatory mental health screening program for students starting this academic year. Under the new policy, all students in grades 7 through 12 will complete confidential mental health assessments twice annually, designed to identify signs of anxiety, depression, and other emotional difficulties. School counselors will then meet individually with students who show concerning results to discuss support options and connect families with community resources. The program was approved by the state legislature last year following data showing a 37 percent increase in student mental health hospitalizations since the pandemic began. Proponents argue that early identification is key to preventing crises and helping students succeed academically. However, some parent groups have raised privacy concerns, though school officials emphasize that all screening results are protected by federal health privacy laws and will not be shared without parental consent. The state has hired 200 additional school counselors to support the program rollout.

transcript.heading: News Report Three (British Female)
paras: Public libraries across Ireland are reporting record participation in this year's summer reading challenge, with over 120,000 children already signed up as of mid-July. The annual program encourages children aged 5 to 12 to read at least six books during the summer holidays, offering stickers, certificates, and small prizes as incentives. Library staff note that participation is up 25 percent compared to last year, which they attribute to an increased focus on diverse book selections and partnerships with popular children's authors. This year's theme, "Space Explorers," features both fiction and non-fiction books about astronomy, space travel, and science. Libraries are also hosting free weekly events including story hours, craft activities, and virtual author visits. Research conducted by the library association shows that children who participate in the summer reading program maintain or improve their reading skills during the break, while non-participants typically experience a decline known as the "summer slide."

6. What is this year's summer reading challenge theme?

transcript.heading: Conversation One (American Male + British Female)
paras: Man (Paul): Hey Sarah, do you have a minute? I was hoping I could ask you for some advice about my job interview tomorrow. I'm really nervous about it.
Woman (Sarah): Of course, Paul! I remember how nervous I was before my first interview after college. What position is it for, again?

Man: It's a marketing assistant position at that software company downtown. I really want this job—the pay is good, and they have a great training program for new graduates. But I'm worried I'll mess up the questions.

Woman: I'm sure you'll do great. The key is preparation. Have you researched the company thoroughly? You should know what their main products are, who their competitors are, and maybe even some recent news about them. They always ask why you want to work there specifically.

Man: Yeah, I've looked at their website and read a few articles about their latest product launch. But I'm not sure how to answer those behavioral questions—you know, the ones where they ask about a time you solved a problem or dealt with a difficult situation.

Woman: Oh right, those use the STAR method: Situation, Task, Action, Result. You should prepare three or four specific stories from your classes, internships, or even part-time jobs that demonstrate different skills—like teamwork, problem-solving, time management. Keep them concise, about a minute each.
Man: That makes sense. What about what to wear? I don't have a suit, just some khakis and a button-down shirt.

Woman: Business casual is probably fine for a marketing assistant role at a tech company, but it's better to be slightly overdressed than underdressed. Your khakis and a nice button-down with clean dress shoes should work. Make sure everything is ironed and you look neat. Also, bring extra copies of your resume in a folder—they might not have printed them out.
Man: Okay, good idea. How early should I arrive? I don't want to be late, but I also don't want to show up too early and make them uncomfortable.

Woman: Ten to fifteen minutes early is perfect. If you get there earlier than that, wait in your car or in the lobby downstairs. And don't forget to send a thank-you email within 24 hours after the interview, reiterating your interest in the position.
Man: Thank you so much, Sarah. That's all really helpful. I feel a bit more confident now.
Woman: You're going to do great! Just remember to smile, make eye contact, and be yourself. They're not just evaluating your skills—they're deciding if you'd be a good fit for their team.
Questions 8 to 11 are based on the conversation you have just heard.
8. What position is Paul interviewing for?
9. According to Sarah, what should Paul prepare for behavioral questions?
10. What does Sarah recommend Paul wear?
11. When does Sarah say Paul should arrive for the interview?

transcript.heading: Conversation Two (British Male + American Female)
paras: Man (William): Hey Amanda, I need your help. My parents' 30th wedding anniversary is coming up next week, and I want to take them somewhere really nice for dinner. Do you have any recommendations?
Woman (Amanda): Oh, that's wonderful, William! Thirty years is a big milestone. What kind of food do your parents like? And what's your budget like? That will help narrow things down.

Man: They're pretty open to different cuisines, but they really enjoy seafood, and they also love Italian food. I'm willing to spend up to 200 dollars total, including drinks and tip. I want it to be a special place, not just a regular chain restaurant.

Woman: Hmm, let me think. There's that new seafood place on the harbor, The Blue Marlin? I went there for my birthday last month, and the food was incredible—fresh oysters, lobster, excellent fish dishes. But it can be pretty pricey. You might be looking at 250 or more with three people and wine.
Man: That sounds a bit over my budget. What about Italian options?

Woman: There's a lovely family-owned Italian place, Giovanni's, in the old town. It's been there for years, very cozy and romantic atmosphere. They make their own pasta, and their tiramisu is amazing. I've taken my own parents there for anniversaries, and they loved it. It's definitely more affordable—probably around 60-70 dollars per person with drinks, so you'd stay within budget easily.
Man: That sounds really nice. Do I need to make a reservation? It's next Saturday evening, so I'm sure it'll be busy.

Woman: Oh, absolutely, you should call them today. Saturday nights fill up fast, especially for a nice place like that. Ask for a table by the window if they have one—it overlooks the little square and has a really charming view. Also, you could mention it's your parents' anniversary when you book—sometimes they bring out a complimentary dessert with a candle.
Man: That's a great tip. What time do you think I should book? They like to eat a bit earlier, not too late.

Woman: Maybe 6:30 or 7 PM? That's early enough that you won't feel rushed, and it's before the main dinner rush. They also have a pre-theater menu until 6:45 that's a bit cheaper, three courses for a fixed price. That could be a good option.
Man: Perfect. I'll give them a call right after class. Should I look at the menu online first to make sure there are options they'll like?
Woman: Definitely. They have the menu posted on their website. They have plenty of seafood pasta options, too, so that should make them happy. Let me know how it goes!
Man: I will. Thanks so much for the recommendation, Amanda!
Questions 12 to 15 are based on the conversation you have just heard.

transcript.heading: Passage One (American Male)
paras: The subscription economy has transformed how consumers access products and services over the past decade, with everything from entertainment and software to groceries and clothing now available through recurring monthly payments. The business model offers several advantages for both companies and consumers. For businesses, subscriptions provide predictable, recurring revenue streams that make financial planning easier and build long-term customer relationships rather than one-time transactions. Data shows that subscription-based companies grow revenue approximately five times faster than traditional product-based businesses. For consumers, subscriptions offer convenience, cost savings on items they use regularly, and the flexibility to access services without large upfront costs—for example, watching unlimited movies on a streaming platform for a monthly fee instead of buying individual DVDs. However, the model has also attracted criticism. Many consumers underestimate how much they spend on subscriptions monthly, with studies showing the average household pays for 12 different subscription services totaling over 200 dollars per month, often for services they rarely use. The auto-renewal feature, in particular, has drawn regulatory attention in many countries, with new laws requiring companies to make cancellation processes clearer and easier. Additionally, some critics argue that subscription models lead to consumers never truly owning products, paying indefinitely for access to software or media they would previously have purchased outright.

transcript.heading: Passage Two (British Female)
paras: Research consistently shows that bilingualism—being able to speak two languages fluently—offers significant cognitive benefits that extend throughout a person's lifetime. Contrary to the old belief that learning two languages simultaneously confused children and slowed their academic development, modern neuroscience has demonstrated that bilingual individuals actually show improved executive function compared to monolinguals. Executive function refers to the set of mental skills that includes working memory, flexible thinking, and self-control. Because bilingual people constantly switch between two language systems in their brains, they develop enhanced ability to focus attention, ignore distractions, and switch between tasks efficiently. These advantages appear early in childhood: bilingual preschoolers have been shown to perform better on problem-solving tasks that require ignoring misleading information. The benefits also persist into old age, with multiple studies finding that bilingual adults develop dementia and Alzheimer's disease an average of four to five years later than monolingual adults, even when brain scans show similar levels of disease-related physical changes. Researchers believe this is due to "cognitive reserve"—the enhanced brain connectivity developed through lifelong bilingualism that helps compensate for age-related decline. It's never too late to benefit from language learning either; adults who learn a second language later in life also show improvements in attention and memory compared to those who remain monolingual.
Questions 20 to 22 are based on the passage you have just heard.
20. What cognitive advantage do bilingual individuals show according to modern research?
21. How much later do bilingual adults typically develop dementia?
22. What concept explains why bilinguals maintain function longer despite brain changes?

transcript.heading: Passage Three (American Female)
paras: Horticultural therapy, the practice of using gardening and plant-related activities to improve physical and mental health, has evolved from a niche alternative treatment to a recognized therapeutic intervention used in hospitals, rehabilitation centers, and senior care facilities around the world. The practice is built on the idea that interacting with plants and nature has inherent healing properties. For individuals recovering from physical injuries or surgery, gardening activities like planting seeds, pulling weeds, and arranging flowers provide low-impact exercise that improves hand strength, coordination, and range of motion. For people experiencing mental health challenges such as depression, anxiety, or post-traumatic stress disorder, gardening offers opportunities for mindfulness, accomplishment, and connection to living things. Studies have found that just 30 minutes of gardening can significantly reduce cortisol levels, the body's primary stress hormone. Horticultural therapy also provides meaningful social connection when done in group settings, reducing feelings of isolation among elderly participants or individuals with disabilities. Unlike many forms of therapy that can feel intimidating or clinical, working with plants feels accessible and non-threatening to most people. Participants often report a sense of purpose and pride from nurturing plants and watching them grow, which can be particularly valuable for individuals struggling with feelings of helplessness or low self-esteem. Many vocational programs now use horticultural therapy to help people with disabilities develop job skills in greenhouse management, landscaping, and floral design.
